# Quantum Bus Parallelism

This repository studies the force, time, and physical-mode resources required
for a layer of disjoint geometric entangling gates through a shared harmonic bus.
The complete scientific account is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, scaling law, direct proof route, reproduction
  command, physical scope, purpose and contact.
- science/model.md: Hamiltonian, exact closure, target matching, local-Z
  equivalence, half-diamond error, force constraints, exact statements and route.
- science/spectral_cost.md: exact weighted spectral action for a prescribed full
  phase matrix, L2/H1 Fourier justification, lower bound and attaining loops.
- science/gate_layer_bounds.md: all-wrap determinant invariant, fixed-error
  phase lifting, perturbation bound and mode-force-time lower bounds.
- science/matching_construction.md: explicit mode, harmonic, sign and quadrature
  allocation, exact gate, peak force, bandwidth and the finite-harmonic boundary.
- science/hardware_resources.md: physical mode counting, longitudinal resonator
  mapping, participation restrictions, bandwidth, excursion and device limits.
- references/related_work.md: primary-source comparisons and attribution of
  imported mathematical methods and established quantum constructions.
- references/references.bib: structured primary bibliography.
- verification/README.md: commands, expected outputs and the limits of checks.
- verification/verify_bus.py: deterministic numerical verification runner.

Reader routes:
- Story: model, gate-layer bounds, matching construction, hardware resources.
- Theorems: model definitions, spectral cost, full gate-layer proofs, construction.
- Hardware interpretation: model assumptions, hardware resources, related work.
- Reproduction: verification guide, code and committed reference output.

Preserve these distinctions:
- K counts disjoint pairs; the number of data qubits is 2K. m counts dynamical
  canonical oscillator modes, not modulation tones or drive envelopes.
- H/hbar=i sum Z_j(u_jl a_l^dagger-u_jl^* a_l), U=exp(i Z^T A Z).
  Off-diagonal pair angle is 2 A_ij; the diagonal of A is only global phase.
- The spectral theorem optimizes a prescribed full A. A physical-gate lower
  bound must also allow diagonal gauges, local Z corrections and phase wraps.
- The fixed-error theorem uses half-diamond error for the entire unitary layer,
  with fixed epsilon<1/sqrt(2), and still requires exact oscillator closure.
- The duration bound charges sum_l |u_jl(t)|^2 <= g^2 separately for each qubit.
  Effective-force fluence is not automatically energy in joules.
- The upper construction is exact and matches scaling order, not every finite
  constant in the lower bound. It assumes independent complex force control.
- The optimal few-mode construction uses growing modulation bandwidth and
  can require growing oscillator excursions; these are not free hardware claims.
- The converse survives hardware control restrictions within the stated model.
  Attainment on a device requires verifying its accessible force functions.
- Intermediate noncommuting spin control, direct qubit interactions, nonlinear
  couplings and active squeezing are not included in the primitive model.
- Approximate rank alone cannot prove the robust cost law: large phase wraps
  can give low-rank approximations at diverging force fluence.
- Classical spectral geometry and parallel entangling constructions are prior
  work. Use references/related_work.md before making an originality claim.
- Finite calculations check their stated cases and normalizations; the written
  proofs establish universal results. Model review is not external peer review.
